Do the outputs concern vulnerable populations or inform emergency response?

questions.hint: For example, an incorrect vegetation-change assessment influencing environmental monitoring results.
questions.text: Could an error affect analytical reliability, interpretation or planning?

questions.hint: Low-tier errors are "readily detectable and correctable".
questions.text: Would an error be hard to detect or to correct?

questions.hint: The degree of autonomy is one of the reasons for a tier.
questions.text: Will outputs be used without a person checking them first?

low.description: Limited consequences, with errors readily detectable and correctable.
low.example: An incorrect land-cover description in an exploratory application with no operational consequences.
triggers: Standard self-assessment with the compliance card

medium.description: Errors may affect analytical reliability, interpretation, or planning, but can be identified and corrected through validation.
medium.example: An incorrect vegetation-change assessment influencing environmental monitoring results.
triggers: Validation to identify and correct errors before use

high.description: Errors could substantially affect safety, critical infrastructure, sensitive information, or consequential decisions.
high.example: Incorrectly identifying flood-exposed infrastructure during emergency response, potentially misleading operational decisions.
triggers: Escalation to the External Advisory Board where needed
